section: 4. Boarding the Orient Express: First Impressions of the Passengers
description: The investigators board the Orient Express, departing from London at 9:10, first-class compartments and various passengers, discussion of costs and actual seating arrangements

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Quick Wait

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: (Should we book three single rooms?)

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Signal for four tickets for a four-person room, all in one room

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Tickets, get daze

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Slightly pained, but this is much better than having a Middle Eastern roommate

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Mentally exclaiming how rich

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: At 9 a.m., platform 2 of Victoria Station suddenly became restless. With a long whistle, the Orient Express slowly pulled into the platform, its dark green carriages gleaming with a steady sheen under the winter sun.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Return to the companions with four tickets, give two tickets to teammates, keep two for myself

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Several noblewomen wearing fur hats paused on the platform, examining the famous luxury train of Europe through their lorgnettes. Second-class passengers crowded by the windows, watching the seeing-off crowd on the platform.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Lead teammates onto the train, holding onto the train door frame while silently praying the boss will reimburse it

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Leave your luggage with the porters, then enter your respective sleeping cars according to your tickets. Meals are served daily in the dining car, and the salon car and chapel car are available around the clock."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: .ra constitution

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Belief arises from desire; if it is what you hope for, it will surely be answered. <player4>'s constitution wish:

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #As soon as getting off the train, tell everyone feeling a bit unwell and rush to the bathroom to vomit

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Porters pushed luggage carts back and forth, wheels grinding over the damp platform. In the distance, a taxi honked, urging newly disembarked passengers. A newsboy ran past, waving the Paris evening paper, his shouts drowned in the noisy crowd.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #After getting off, first buy an evening paper and briefly look at recent local events

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Walk out of the bathroom looking pale

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Step off the train with luggage, looking at player4 beside with an expression saying "bro, don't die in front of me"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "It's fine, minor issue. Health is important."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The newsboy takes your money and hands you the evening paper.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Stop the newsboy, give him money for a newspaper, and ask him in French

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: **Weather & Traffic**

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Take a sip of water, take out Professor Smith's booklet and flip through his notes

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Hey kid, do you know where there's a place to stay?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Sir, you've asked the right person! Walk along this Boulevard Haussmann, turn right at the third intersection—see that green gas lamp? 'Old Mosaic Inn' is 20 francs a night, hot water extra 5 sous! If that's too expensive, across the alley there's 'Three Pigeons,' the landlady is my aunt, mention little Jacques' name and she'll knock off 3 coins..."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Alright, why not?" #Give him money for another newspaper

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: He deftly takes the coin, bites it to check, grins.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Sir, ask him about Count Fenanik."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Too late."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Hmm, perhaps we should start by learning about this Count."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "I think that should be something we can look up at the library."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Shall we go, then? To the library first?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "And why do you think some kid on the street would know anything about a Count?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Let's go then."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Take out the pocket watch to check the current time.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: It is already 9:50 PM.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Look at that Ritz Hotel in the newspaper."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Looks nice. Hope it doesn't get smashed by extremists." Strokes chin.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Indicate that either option is fine.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #wegokuwegoku

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I think the one the newsboy recommended is good."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: A capped driver leans against the polished black Citroën B12's door, the ember of his cigarette flickering in the cold night. Spotting you with suitcases exiting the station, he immediately stubs out the cigarette, grinds it with his boot heel, and strides over—

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Even without understanding French, the meaning of the person in front is perfectly clear.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: A carriage driver suddenly walks over. "Don't listen to this tin can's nonsense! Ride my 'Victoria' open carriage at night—" He lifts a blanket. "Hot bricks wrapped up! Go down the Champs-Élysées, the Christmas lights haven't been taken down yet, 25 francs and includes commentary!" Then he pulls out a yellowed photo. "Look, I even drove Monsieur Proust last week!"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: That must be the driver.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The car driver mocks, "Give it a rest, old Henri! Your 'Lightning' almost gave up the ghost on the Montmartre slope yesterday..." He then turns and winks at you. "Tell you what, a discount for you, 26 francs—"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Considering we've taken too many cars in America, head towards the carriage with the luggage.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The car driver dramatically snatches off his cap, pressing it to his chest in an exaggerated gesture of heartbreak. "Ah! You're cutting my flesh with a blunt knife!" He suddenly turns and kicks a tire. The Citroën lets out a piercing alarm. "This hunk of iron might go hungry tonight!"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "We're not that interested in Christmas lights."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Ha! A sensible one!" He suddenly sticks the whip into his boot top and pulls out a greasy map from under the seat. "Then we'll take 'Rat Alley'—"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Get seated.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "By the way, as an old Frenchman, sir, have you heard of Count Fenanik?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Fenanik? Never heard of him."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Look at Bailan and player4, switch to English. "Do you have anything you want to ask?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The carriage driver scratches his graying temple, the whip tip unconsciously tracing a circle in the air.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Ask if there are any local strange happenings."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "That name sounds like someone from those old oil paintings in the museum!"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "That is indeed good advice. Do you know the way?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The horse's hooves clatter briskly on the cobblestones. The driver hums an old folk song.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "That's very kind of you."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "My friend said he really likes your service."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The coachman's eyes light up. He takes off his hat, presses it to his chest, and gives an exaggerated bow. "Thank you!" he shouts in a thick accent, his whip tracing a cheerful circle in the air.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Take a look at the attraction markers on the map.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "For a chartered price..." "He draws numbers in the air with his whip." "80 francs a day, includes the horse but not meals—" Then he suddenly lowers his voice and winks. "But if you compliment Lightning's mane a bit more... I can drop it to 75!"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "I've always thought animals are much better than those steel monsters."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Upon hearing this, the coachman immediately beams, even the wrinkles on his face smoothing out.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Although some people value their cars more than their wives, I'd say they still can't compare to a real partner."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "This old fellow has been with me for twelve years, never left me stranded on the road—unlike those iron toads that keep coughing and going on strike!"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Then you should buy him some good fodder." #Quietly takes out the 5 pounds exchanged earlier from own wallet and hands it to him.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: He stares at the pound note, his Adam's apple bobbing. "Sir, this is enough to buy Lightning alfalfa for a year!"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Wow."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Greet politely in English.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The front desk receptionist, wearing a crisp black uniform with a small golden key pin on his collar, is looking down organizing the register. Hearing footsteps, he immediately looks up with a professional smile.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Yes, please, thank you!"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Very much needed."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Right away." Three crisp bell rings, and he simultaneously whispers a few quick words in French. In an instant, two impeccably uniformed attendants quietly appear in the lobby. "Pierre will show you to your rooms—" He turns to a younger attendant. "And the hot chocolate and macarons will arrive at the same time as you."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Then one double room and one single room, please."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: He turns and retrieves two brass keys from the teak key cabinet. "Double room number 16 on the third floor, and single room number 18 next door."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Step forward and leave own personal information, signing Bailan Sha on the registration form.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Fill out the form.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Write Patteo's signature on the registration form.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Simultaneously shows an admiring expression towards the professor's title.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Parfait." (Perfect.) The receptionist files the registration form in a folder. "Please follow Pierre to your rooms."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "You admire that title?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Let's go. How about we meet in the lobby tomorrow at 8 AM?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "All doctoral students want to become professors, right?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Not for me."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Professor, you are truly accomplished for your age."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "It's just a title. Don't let it constrain you too much. Perhaps after this journey, the achievements you gain..."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Mhm, Professor, you're right. I've learned from you."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "To the best of my knowledge, there is a truly accomplished individual who, for some reason, just can't seem to get the recognition they deserve."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The waiters maintained a perfectly measured distance, standing by silently like finely tuned clocks.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Haha, is that really the case?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "You're not from the archaeology department; if you were, you'd know him."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Well, good luck then."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "That person could easily get the title just by speaking up a little, but for some reason, they're oddly principled about this."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Perhaps they just don't want to be bound by that title."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "If they didn't want to be bound, they wouldn't still be holed up at the university."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The waiter gave a slight bow, a faint smile on his lips, his voice as soft as a feather.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Thank you very much. I'll head in to rest now."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Go into the room, and also tip a little.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #First, go in and tidy up a bit, then look at the scenery outside the window.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Thanks for your hard work."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: As Pierre took the tip, his wrist turned slightly, and the coin vanished into his sleeve as if performing a small magic trick. "Thank you, sir! May your dreams tonight be sweeter than our macarons." Fine wrinkles appeared at the corners of his smiling eyes as he took half a step back and bowed gracefully before leaving.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "player4, have a macaron."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Wash up briefly, then get ready to rest.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Dig in.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #First toss a chocolate-flavored one into my mouth, then throw the pistachio one to player4.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The crisp shell shed crumbs at the slightest touch; biting into it revealed rich dark chocolate, stirring a storm on the tongue—the bitterness of Venezuelan cocoa tamed by honey, the aftertaste like velvet brushing the throat.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Exclaiming, "I never thought attending a lecture would give me the chance to tour Europe."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The rose-flavored one carried the ambiguity of Persian spices; the pistachio filling exuded the oily fragrance of Sicilian sunshine.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Too sweet." #Sip some hot chocolate.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I think it's alright? Maybe something sweet helps settle the stomach after motion sickness."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "That's the best."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Professor Bailan wiped the last droplets of water from her face with a plush towel, the steam from the bathroom forming a mist behind her. The fluffy texture of the towel felt like burying her face in a freshly sun-dried quilt. The goose-down duvet on the bed carried a faint scent of incense. As she reached to turn off the bedside lamp, she noticed a fresh rose on the nightstand. In the darkness, the outline of the petals gradually became clear, as if floating in the night.
